topic.title: Attention Expressivity, Priors, and Computational Efficiency
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Attention mechanisms decide how information from different tokens is combined. This cluster examines their representational capacity, low-rank restrictions, sparsity, pooling, and efficient approximations. A representative method groups less relevant tokens to reduce redundant computation, while another interprets attention as an optimal-transport problem with a learnable prior.
topic.whyItMatters: Long contexts make attention expensive, but reducing computation can also remove information or restrict what a model can represent. Studying capacity and inductive assumptions alongside runtime helps explain when an approximation preserves the behavior that matters.
topic.evolution: Early representatives apply attention to speech and sequence tasks. Later papers analyze multi-head bottlenecks and linear-time alternatives. Recent work connects attention to coding, transport, and universal approximation, while investigating attention sinks and length extrapolation as architectural questions.
openQuestions: Which efficient attention mechanisms preserve rare but decisive long-range interactions?
Can learned attention priors generalize to substantially longer or structurally different inputs?
